stem.text: Sand is added to a pile at a work site at the rate \( r(t) = 16 \cos{\left(\frac{\pi t}{4} \right)} + 9 \) tons per hour, and removed at the constant rate of 7 tons per hour, for \( 0 \le t \le 8 \). At time \( t = 0 \) there are 150 tons of sand in the pile, and t is measured in hours. Using a calculator, find the time in \( 0 \le t \le 8 \) at which the amount A(t) of sand is greatest, and justify the answer. Show the setup for the calculations.

answer_key.label: The amount is greatest at t = 2.160, where A is 174.531 tons, the largest of the values of A at t = 0, at both critical points and at t = 8.

worked_solution.text: The amount is \( A(t) = 150 + \int_{0}^{t} \left(16 \cos{\left(\frac{\pi s}{4} \right)} + 2\right)\,ds \), so \( A'(t) = r(t) - 7 = 16 \cos{\left(\frac{\pi t}{4} \right)} + 2 \). Setting \( A'(t) = 0 \) and solving with a calculator gives \( t = 2.160 \) and \( t = 5.840 \) in the interval.
worked_solution.rule_named: critical points of an accumulation function

worked_solution.text: The candidates are the critical points and both endpoints: \( A(0) = 150 \), \( A(2.160) \approx 174.531 \), \( A(5.840) \approx 141.469 \), and \( A(8) = 150 + \int_{0}^{8} A'(s)\,ds = 166 \).
The largest candidate value is about 174.531, at the first critical point, so the amount is greatest at \( t = 2.160 \) hours.
